objectives: Name the three main types of soil and describe them.
Say what humus is and why it is useful.
Explain what soil erosion is and how to reduce it.
reviewNotes: Soil types simplified to three; check regional soil names (e.g. volcanic soils near Mount Cameroon).

blocks.title: Types of soil
blocks.md: **Sandy soil** has big grains; water runs through it quickly. **Clay soil** has tiny sticky grains; it holds a lot of water and is used for bricks and pots. **Loam** is a mix of sand, clay and **humus**, and it is the best for farming. **Humus** is made from rotted plants and animals and gives plants food.

blocks.caption: Three types of soil.
blocks.alt: A table with sand, clay and loam: size of grains, how much water they hold, and what they are good for.

blocks.title: Erosion
blocks.md: **Soil erosion** is when rain or wind carries away the top layer of soil. It happens most on **bare, sloping land** after trees and plants are cut. We can reduce it by **planting trees and grass**, **covering the soil** with leaves or crops, and planting across a slope instead of down it.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Thinking that soil is the same everywhere: different places have different soils.
- Saying that clay is best for plants because it holds water: loam is best.
- Cutting all trees on a hill, which leads to erosion.
- Burning dry leaves instead of using them as compost.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Ako pours 200 ml of water on sandy soil and 120 ml drips out. How much water stayed in the soil?
steps: Water that stayed = water poured − water that came out.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Which soil would you use to make pots? Why?
steps: The soil must be sticky and keep its shape when wet.
Clay: its tiny grains stick together.

blocks.title: The water cycle
blocks.md: The Sun **heats** water in the sea, rivers and lakes and some of it becomes an invisible gas, **water vapour** (**evaporation**). Vapour rises, cools and turns into tiny drops that form **clouds** (**condensation**). When the drops get heavy they fall as **rain** (**precipitation**). Rain runs into rivers and the sea, and the cycle starts again.

blocks.caption: The water cycle.
blocks.alt: A diagram with the sea and the land. Arrows show evaporation going up from the sea under the sun, condensation making a cloud, rain falling on the land and water running back to rivers and the sea.

blocks.title: Using and cleaning water
blocks.md: We use water for **drinking, cooking, washing, farming and industry**. Water sources are rain, rivers, springs, wells and boreholes. To make drinking water **safe**: let dirt settle, **filter** it through clean cloth, then **boil** it for a few minutes or use a treatment advised by a health worker. Do not waste water.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Thinking that clouds are smoke: they are tiny drops of water.
- Saying that water disappears when it evaporates: it becomes water vapour in the air.
- Thinking that clear water is always safe: germs cannot be seen.
- Throwing rubbish into rivers.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Why does wet washing dry on a sunny day?
steps: The Sun's heat makes the water in the cloth evaporate.
The water turns into water vapour and goes into the air.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: What happens when water vapour rises and cools?
steps: Cool air makes the vapour turn back into tiny drops.
This is condensation and the drops make clouds.

blocks.title: Weather
blocks.md: **Weather** is what the air is like at a place and time: **sunny, cloudy, rainy, windy, hot or cold**. We measure the **temperature** with a **thermometer** (in degrees Celsius, °C), the **rain** with a rain gauge (in mm) and the **wind direction** with a wind vane. **Climate** is the usual weather over many years.

blocks.caption: Rain recorded in five months (an imaginary village).
blocks.alt: A bar chart of rain in millimetres: January 15, February 40, March 110, April 160, May 95.

blocks.title: Seasons in Cameroon
blocks.md: Most of Cameroon has two seasons: the **dry season** (little rain, sunny, dusty Harmattan wind in the north) and the **rainy season** (clouds, heavy rain). The south has **two rainy seasons** a year, the north **one**. Weather changes the way we dress, farm and travel: umbrellas in the rain, light clothes in the heat.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Mixing **weather** (today) with **climate** (over many years).
- Reading a thermometer at the wrong level: read the top of the liquid.
- Thinking that it always rains in the rainy season: it also has sunny periods.
- Forgetting the unit °C.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: In the chart, which month had the most rain and how much more than January?
steps: The tallest bar is April: 160 mm. January had 15 mm.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Find the average rain in the five months.
